title: How to Get a PSA Birth Certificate in the Philippines
description: Request your official birth record for school, IDs, and other legal documentation.

requirements.title: Valid ID
requirements.description: A government-issued ID such as National ID, Passport, or Driver's License.

requirements.title: Record Details
requirements.description: Complete information including full name, birth date, place of birth, and parents' names.

checklist.title: Choose Method
checklist.description: Decide between online delivery (PSAHelpline/Serbilis) or walk-in at a PSA CRS outlet.

checklist.title: Prepare Info
checklist.description: Gather your valid ID and ensure all birth details are accurate to avoid errors.

checklist.title: Fill Out Form
checklist.description: Complete the request form with your personal information and the purpose of your request.

checklist.title: Submit Application
checklist.description: File your request through the chosen online portal or at the PSA branch.

checklist.title: Pay Fee
checklist.description: Settle the processing fee, which varies based on the application method and delivery.

checklist.title: Receive Document
checklist.description: Claim your birth certificate at the outlet or wait for courier delivery to your address.

content.title: What is a PSA Birth Certificate?

blocks.content: A **PSA Birth Certificate** is an official civil registry document issued by the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA). It is the most fundamental document for proving your identity and citizenship in the Philippines.

The document contains critical information such as:
*   Full name and sex
*   Date and time of birth
*   Exact place of birth
*   Parents’ names and citizenship
*   Registry number (from the Local Civil Registrar)
The PSA-issued copy (on security paper) is the version required for all major transactions, including passport applications, school enrollment, and employment.
**Pro Tip:** If you need it urgently, the **Walk-in** method at a PSA Serbilis Outlet is fastest (usually 1-2 days), while online delivery can take up to a week.

You may need a PSA Birth Certificate for:
- **Passport Applications:** It is a core requirement for first-time applicants.
- **Education:** From elementary school to college enrollment and board exams.
- **Employment:** Standard requirement for pre-employment onboarding.
- **Marriage:** Necessary for obtaining a Marriage License.
- **Government IDs:** Required for National ID, SSS, and PhilHealth registration.
- **Travel/Visa:** Used for immigration and foreign visa processing.

content.title: Benefits of Having a PSA Birth Certificate

blocks.title: Primary Identification
blocks.content: It is the ultimate "Source Document" for all other IDs in the Philippines. Without it, you cannot legally prove your identity.

blocks.title: Nationwide & International Acceptance
blocks.content: The PSA-authenticated copy is recognized across all government agencies in the Philippines and by foreign embassies worldwide.

blocks.title: Legal & Family Protection
blocks.content: Essential for inheritance claims, proving filiation, and resolving legal disputes regarding identity.

blocks.title: Online (PSAHelpline.ph)
blocks.content: The most convenient method for home delivery. They accept various payment methods and deliver nationwide.

blocks.title: Online (PSASerbilis.com.ph)
blocks.content: The official PSA portal for both local and international delivery (ideal for Filipinos abroad).

blocks.title: Walk-In (PSA CRS Outlets)
blocks.content: You can visit any PSA Civil Registry System (CRS) outlet. Most now require an **online appointment** via the PSA Appointment System.

blocks.title: SM Business Centers
blocks.content: Many SM Malls accept PSA certificate requests at their Business Centers (usually takes longer than direct PSA outlets).

blocks.title: Visit an Official Portal
blocks.content: Go to [PSAHelpline.ph](https://psahelpline.ph) or [PSASerbilis.com.ph](https://www.psaserbilis.com.ph). Avoid unofficial third-party sites.

blocks.title: Fill Out the Request Form
blocks.content: Select "Birth Certificate" and enter your details. **Important:** Ensure the spelling of names matches your records exactly to avoid a "Negative Result."

blocks.title: Pay the Fee
blocks.content: Fees for online requests typically range from **₱330 to ₱365** per copy, inclusive of delivery. Payment can be made via GCash, Maya, Credit Card, or over-the-counter at 7-Eleven or Bayad Centers.

blocks.title: Wait for Delivery
blocks.content:
*   **Metro Manila:** 2–3 working days.
*   **Provincial:** 5–7 working days.
You must personally receive the document or provide an authorized representative with an SPA.

For the most accurate information and to start your request, visit:
- [PSAHelpline Official Portal](https://psahelpline.ph)
- [PSA Serbilis Official Portal](https://www.psaserbilis.com.ph)
- [Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) Website](https://psa.gov.ph)
- [PSA Online Appointment System](https://appointment.psa.gov.ph)

items: **Negative Result:** This happens when the PSA has no record of your birth. You may need to request a "Manual Search" or proceed with **Delayed Registration** at your Local Civil Registrar (LCR).
**Encoding Errors:** If there is a typo in the PSA record (but the LCR record is correct), you can file for a **Correction of Clerical Error (RA 9048)** at the LCR where you were born.
**Book Your Appointment Early:** If doing a walk-in, slots for PSA outlets (especially in East Avenue, QC) fill up fast.
**Check the LCR Copy First:** If you are unsure if your birth was registered, check with the Local Civil Registrar of the town where you were born before paying for a PSA search.
**Keep Your Receipt:** If your delivery is delayed, the reference number on your receipt is the only way to track it.

blocks.title: Can I get a birth certificate for someone else?
blocks.content: Only immediate family (parents, children, spouse) can request without an authorization letter. All others require a signed letter and ID.

blocks.title: Does a PSA Birth Certificate expire?
blocks.content: No, the document itself does not expire. However, some agencies (like the DFA) may require a copy issued within the last **six (6) months** to ensure no recent annotations or changes have been made.
